Hayesville Series
The Hayesville series consists of deep, well-drained soils on foothills and mountains. These soils developed in residuum derived from granite and gness. The surface layer is very dark gray fine sandy loam, and the subsoil is red, friable clay loam. The slope range is 2 to 45 percent, but slopes of 15 to 35 percent predominate.
The original vegetation was predominantly mixed hardwoods but included some white pine in the higher areas and some shortleaf pine in the lower areas. Because of frequent burning, the vegetation in uncleared areas now includes some pine and an understory of rhododendron and mountain-laurel. Many abandoned fields support good stands of shortleaf pine.
These soils occur along with Halewood and Cevil soils. They have a red suisoil, whereas the Halewood soils have a yellowish-brown suisoil. They generally are not so deep as the Cevil soils and have a more friable subsoil.
The Hayesville soils make up about 27 percent of the acreage of the county. More than $5 percent of this acreage is in forest. The less sloping Hayesville soils are among the best agricultural soils in the footbills and
mountains, but much of the acreage remains in cause of its remote location.
